why: DFS that passes state down: each child receives the path string built so far, and a leaf emits it. It also shows the backtracking view: the path grows on the way down and shrinks on the way back.
hints: What does a node need to know from above to write its full root-to-leaf path?
Pass the path so far into each child (path + '->' + child value). When you reach a node with no children, add the path to the answer.
Recursive DFS, or for a 100000-deep tree a stack of (node, path) pairs; push the right child before the left so the left subtree is finished first.
pitfalls: A single node is itself a leaf: return ["1"].
Negative values keep their minus sign: "-1->-2".
With an explicit stack, pushing left before right reverses the required left-to-right order.
